notes: MONEY DATED TO A LATER MONTH WAS LANDING IN THIS MONTH'S CLOSE AS WELL AS ITS OWN. REPORTED: salary received on 31 October but dated 1 November, as the user always logs it, pushed October's closing cash to about Rs 4.5 lakh when the savings account held about Rs 2.9 lakh. ROOT CAUSE: applyTransactionDelta never looks at tx.date, so logging a transaction moves the account balance immediately whatever month it is dated to. That is correct for the Account Balances row at the top of the sheet, which reports what is actually in the account right now and is the reason those live rows exist. It is wrong for a month-end CLOSE, which must contain only what belongs to that month. The Rs 2,66,000 therefore sat inside October's close via the live balance AND would arrive again as November income — the same money counted in two months. FIXED: the current month's close now strips the net effect of every transaction dated beyond that month before using the live balances. All types are handled, not just income, so a forward-dated expense, transfer, contribution, redemption or adjustment cannot skew the close either; liability-account adjustments keep their inverted sign. The top Account Balances row is deliberately unchanged and still shows the true live balance, which is the distinction the user asked for: live balances report reality, the close reports the month. Verified: with and without a Rs 2,66,000 next-month salary logged against an account balance that already contains it, October closes at Rs 2,11,662 either way. ALSO RENAMED: the bottom row read 'Savings (end of month)' while reporting savings PLUS the salary account, net of the card. Labelling it Savings invited comparison against the savings balance alone, a smaller number, and made a correct figure look wrong. It now reads 'Cash at end of month — savings + salary account, after the card is settled'. WARNING ADDED: when income is dated to a later month, the section header states the amount and explains that it appears in the live balances above but is held out of this month's close and counted in the month it belongs to. The figure is no longer silently different from what the balances suggest. CHECKED AND NOT A BUG: an EMI closed early still reports as active in its close month. _emiEndIso returns the close month and _emiActiveIn treats it as inclusive, so the month in which the loan was closed is correctly the last one charged — the October EMI had genuinely been paid. It reads inactive from the following month. LEFT AS REQUESTED: borrowing recorded as ad-hoc income, which raises net worth by the borrowed amount since no liability account exists for it; and the budget-held rule for spending still to come. Regression confirms the Projection-to-Dashboard and Decisions-to-chain gaps both remain zero. No page errors.
